10: - index.html — self-contained animated visual guide. Open directly in any modern browser.
11: - tokens.css — production tokens and small reusable component styles.

16: ## Color
17: Light: canvas #FAFAFA, surface #FFFFFF, raised #F4F4F4, text #171717, secondary #666666, border #DEDEDE. Dark: canvas #111111, surface #1A1A1A, raised #242424, text #F5F5F5, secondary #AAAAAA, border #383838. Black and white establish the identity; grays express hierarchy. Use text and icons for success, warning and error; no color-only status. Never place small gray labels over animated orb lines.
18: 
19: ## Typography
20: System sans: SF on Apple; Segoe UI on Windows; system fallback elsewhere. No font downloads required. Product wordmark: Orbs, medium, -0.04em; use text rather than a fabricated logo asset.
21: Display 48/52 weight 500, -0.04em (mobile 36/40). Section 28/34 weight 500, -0.025em. Card title 18/24 weight 600, -0.015em. Body 15/22 weight 400. Control 14/20 weight 500. 42: Listening pulse is the approved illustrative rhythm, not microphone-driven. Render it only while recording. If implementing audio reactivity later, replace its wrapper scale with normalized RMS, clamped to .88–1.2; leave breathing geometry intact. Hero slot needs 12px motion clearance on each side (64 × 1.2 = 76.8px). Inline orb sits inside a minimum 44px pill. Motion changes have a distinct rhythm, rather than speed alone.
43: 
44: State path: Idle → Listening → Thinking → Acting → Confirmation (for writes) → Acting → Done. Cancel returns Idle; failure enters Error. User correction can return Listening. Read-only results may go Acting → Done directly. No fake progress, fabricated success, or invented completion percentages. After 8s show 'Still checking…'; after 20s show cancel/retry if backend supports it. Keep truthful text when tools take longer.
45: 
46: ## Cards
47: 1. Context: small source chip + user's interpreted request; edit/change target available.
48: 2. Result: one sentence outcome; up to three information rows; source attribution.
49: 3. Confirmation: summarize exact writes and affected objects; primary Confirm, secondary Cancel.
50: 4. Done: report confirmed changes; Undo only if backend provides reversal.
51: 5. Error: what failed, preserved context, Retry/Cancel.
52: Desktop: anchored 12px from target, flip to keep 16px viewport margin; clamp to viewport, close on Escape and restore trigger focus. Mobile: bottom contextual sheet above keyboard and safe area with 16px side margins. No dim backdrop for passive results; modal confirmation may use 20% black scrim, dialog semantics and trapped focus. Scroll result content when height exceeds 60vh. Voice transcript remains editable; text input remains available.
53: 
54: ## Motion
55: Enter: 320ms cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), opacity 0→1, y 8→0px, scale .98→1. Exit: 160ms cubic-bezier(.4,0,1,1), opacity 1→0, y 0→4px. State change: 200ms cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1). Control feedback:120ms. Native equivalents can use cubic timing curves; avoid spring overshoot. Orbs can loop linearly internally; never bounce the whole card. Animate transforms/opacity; pause offscreen. Reduced motion: static orb, persistent textual state, immediate placement with optional 100ms opacity fade. No essential state conveyed only through animation.
56: 
57: ## Accessibility
58: Visible labels for all states. role=status / aria-live=polite for status text, not a per-frame announcement. Canvas aria-hidden when adjacent text duplicates it. Modal confirmation uses role=dialog, labelled title, focus trap, Escape and restored focus. Keyboard selection offers same context as hover. Maintain body contrast ≥4.5:1; large text ≥3:1. Focus ring 2px with 3px offset. Debug attention layer pointer-events:none. Microphone button has explicit accessible name and recording state. Do not auto-record.

60: ## Using the selected exact library component
61: npm install thinking-orbs@0.3.2 react react-dom
62: 
63: ```tsx
64: import { OrbsIndicator } from './OrbsIndicator';
65: <OrbsIndicator state="thinking" size={64} dark={false} reducedMotion={false} />
66: ```
67: 
68: OrbsIndicator imports orb-motion.css. Internally it always renders <ThinkingOrb state="breathing" size={64} /> (or 20) with state-specific speed and dotSize props. Theme is theme="dark" / theme="light". Supply reducedMotion from your app's hook; the CSS also honors the OS preference. All wrappers stop for confirmation, done and error. Use check/warning icons and visible text beside them. The standalone guide bundles React and the exact library and opens offline. MIT notices included. No custom geometry renderer remains.

1: # Frontend: Orb Agent (iPhone app)
2: 
3: The visible app name is Orb Agent; the Xcode project, target and bundle ID stay `BeaverAgent`.
4: 
5: WP1 from [docs/work-packages.md](../docs/work-packages.md).
6: The WebSocket, Cards and A2UI sections of [docs/contracts.md](../docs/contracts.md) are the API.
7: 
8: ## Build and run
9: 
10: Open `BeaverAgent/BeaverAgent.xcodeproj` in Xcode and run the `BeaverAgent` scheme, or build from the command line:
11: 
12: ```sh
13: xcodebuild -project frontend/BeaverAgent/BeaverAgent.xcodeproj -scheme BeaverAgent \
14:   -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17 Pro' -derivedDataPath ./.derived build
15: ```
16: 
17: For the demo iPhone, pick your own team under Signing & Capabilities.
18: 
19: `a2ui-swift` is pinned to upstream revision `16476ba`, not `from: "0.3.0"`.
20: Every 0.3.x tag depends on `swift-foundation-icu` by revision, which SwiftPM refuses under a version requirement, and that commit drops the dependency.
21: Move back to a version rule once a tag after 0.3.5 is released.
22: 
23: ## Modes
24: 
25: The app starts in fixture mode ("Demo data"): typed questions replay the bundled fixtures as server frames, through the same decoding and rendering path as live frames.
26: Questions about flights, events or the week return the event and flight cards; anything else returns the demo reply.
27: Turn off "Use demo data" in settings and enter the tunnel URL and `APP_TOKEN` to go live.
28: 
29: The keyboard button next to the orb opens a sheet to type a question (the `text` frame).
30: In fixture mode, touching and holding the orb opens the same sheet, and the sheet can pretend a screenshot arrived, which shows the screen chip.
31: 
32: ## Voice
33: 
34: Live, the orb is push-to-talk: hold it and talk, let go to send.
35: A touch shorter than 250 ms is a tap: it stops the mascot (`interrupt`) instead of starting a question.
36: The mic audio from the moment the finger went down is kept and sent once the touch counts as a hold, so the first word is not lost.
37: 
38: "Hands-free" in settings reconnects with `mode: "handsfree"`: the mic streams the whole time, also while the mascot speaks, and the server decides when a turn ends.
39: Talking over the mascot makes the server send `state: listening`, and the app stops playback at once.
40: 
41: `VoiceIO.swift` follows contracts § Audio: `.playAndRecord` with `.defaultToSpeaker`, voice processing on, mic converted to Int16 24 kHz mono and sent as 3840-byte chunks, TTS played on an `AVAudioPlayerNode` on the same engine.
42: The orb shows `speaking` while TTS audio is still queued, even after the server's `state: idle`.
43: After an interrupt, the rest of the cancelled turn's audio is dropped until the next turn's `state: thinking`.
44: The console logs one line per reply (`voice: reply played, … underruns`) and every stop (`voice: playback stopped …`).
45:

85: The orb shows `speaking` while the app still has audio queued, even after the server has sent `state: idle`.
86: 
87: **Interrupting.** A new press (its first `audio` frame), a `text`, or an `interrupt` cancels the running turn: the agent call and the TTS stream. A cancelled turn sends no `audio_end`. After `interrupt` the server sends `state: idle` only if it cancelled a running turn; after a new press, `state: listening`. Gradium generates speech faster than real time, so seconds of audio may already be queued in the app. The app must stop playback the moment it interrupts, without waiting for `state: idle`, and drop `audio` frames until the next `reply`.
88: 
89: **Hands-free mode.** Opt in with `"mode": "handsfree"` in `hello`; push-to-talk stays the default. The app streams `audio` for as long as it is connected, also while the mascot speaks, and never sends `audio_end`, so echo cancellation must be on (see [Audio](#audio)) or the mascot hears itself and cuts itself off. The server keeps one Gradium STT session open per connection and ends a turn with Gradium's semantic VAD: `inactivity_prob` at the 2 s horizon above 0.5 for 3 steps in a row, once the turn has words. Then it flushes, sends `transcript` and runs the turn as usual. The first words of each turn cancel the running turn, as a new press does, and send `state: listening`. The server's turn is often over while the app still plays queued audio, so in this mode `state: listening` is the app's cue to stop playback and drop `audio` until the next `reply`. Each hands-free connection holds an STT session the whole time, even in silence, which counts against Gradium's concurrent session limit.

100: ## Audio
101: 
102: Both directions use Gradium's native format, so the server forwards the base64 strings without decoding them.
103: 
104: | Direction | Format | Gradium side |
105: | --- | --- | --- |
106: | Mic, app → server | PCM signed 16-bit little-endian, mono, 24 kHz; 80 ms chunks = 1920 samples = 3840 bytes | STT setup `input_format: "pcm"` |
107: | TTS, server → app | Same format, chunks as Gradium sends them | TTS setup `output_format: "pcm_24000"` (the default `pcm` is 48 kHz) |
108: 
109: **iPhone side:** audio session `.playAndRecord` with `.defaultToSpeaker`, or iOS plays through the quiet earpiece while the mic is on. Turn on echo cancellation with `inputNode.setVoiceProcessingEnabled(true)` before reading the input format. Convert the input with `AVAudioConverter` to Int16 at 24 kHz mono. Play through an `AVAudioPlayerNode` on the same engine, converting each chunk to a Float32 24 kHz buffer.
110: 
111: **Gradium facts the server relies on** ([docs](https://docs.gradium.ai/api-reference/introduction)): auth header `x-api-key`; STT at `wss://api.gradium.ai/api/speech/asr`, TTS at `wss://api.gradium.ai/api/speech/tts`; the Python SDK is `pip install gradium`. STT needs `json_config.language` (`en` for the demo, `any` to auto-detect). STT sends `text` segments, not partial and final flags. On push-to-talk release the server sends `flush`, waits for `flushed`, and joins the segments into the transcript. TTS has no cancel message: closing the socket stops it. The free plan allows 2 TTS and 3 STT sessions at once, which is tight with 3 devs testing; the $13 XS plan raises that to 5 and 20.

203: 
204: class Reply(TypedDict):
205:     say: str          # one or two short sentences, the user's language
206:     cards: list[dict] # see Cards

208: class Agent:
209:     async def start(self) -> None:
